findings: No sustained arrhythmia. No pauses greater than 2 seconds. No AV block.

csf.interpretation: Unremarkable CSF. Normal cell count, protein, and glucose.

additional_observations: No mass, midline shift or hydrocephalus
ct.impression: Non-contrast CT head: no acute intracranial abnormality. Impression: normal non-contrast CT of the head.

findings: Structurally normal heart. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. No pericardial effusion.

background.pdr: 9-10 Hz posterior dominant rhythm, symmetric and reactive
background.sleep_features: normal vertex waves and sleep spindles

eeg.impression: Normal awake and drowsy EEG. No epileptiform discharges and no focal slowing.

findings.description: 3 Hz trains of 10 stimuli; skin temperature 33 C; no anticholinesterase medication taken.
Baseline CMAP 2.3 mV; decrement 1st to 4th response 13%.
Baseline CMAP 9.4 mV; decrement 4%. After 10 s maximal contraction CMAP 9.6 mV; no facilitation.

output.impression: 1. Decrement of 11-13% at 3 Hz in facial muscles (nasalis, orbicularis oculi). 2. No decrement in abductor digiti minimi; normal baseline CMAP amplitudes; no post-exercise facilitation. Findings are consistent with a postsynaptic disorder of neuromuscular transmission affecting cranial muscles. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.description: 20 fiber pairs. Mean MCD 46 microseconds (reference <35). Increased jitter in 9 of 20 pairs (45%); blocking in 8% of pairs.

output.impression: Abnormal single-fiber EMG of the frontalis: increased jitter with impulse blocking, consistent with a disorder of neuromuscular transmission. Clinical correlation recommended.
FVC 2.77 L (94% predicted, 47 mL/kg), MIP -74 cmH2O and MEP 86 cmH2O within reference limits; effective cough. Normal respiratory muscle function.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: AChR binding antibody 1.11 nmol/L with elevated blocking antibody; MuSK negative; TSH and free T4 normal
action_criteria.label: Order AChR binding antibody and thyroid function
action_criteria.rationale: Hypophonia that fades through the day and with sustained phonation after a normal laryngoscopy points to fatigable laryngeal weakness; AChR binding antibody is the first-line test and TSH screens for thyroid disease (Jacob S et al., Pract Neurol 2025; Evoli A et al., Neurol Sci 2019).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Decrement of 13% in nasalis and 11% in orbicularis oculi, none in ADM; normal CMAPs, no facilitation
action_criteria.label: Order repetitive nerve stimulation including facial muscles
action_criteria.rationale: With cranial-only weakness, RNS must include facial muscles (nasalis, orbicularis oculi), where the decrement is most likely (Jacob S et al., Pract Neurol 2025).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No anterior mediastinal mass; thymic involution appropriate for age
action_criteria.label: Order mediastinal CT with contrast to look for thymoma
action_criteria.rationale: Thymic imaging is indicated in every patient with MG; at 53 with AChR-positive bulbar (generalized) MG it also decides thymectomy (Jacob S et al., Pract Neurol 2025; MGTX).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: FVC 94% predicted (47 mL/kg), MIP -74 and MEP 86 cmH2O, effective cough
action_criteria.label: Measure baseline respiratory function (FVC, MIP, MEP)
action_criteria.rationale: Laryngeal and palatal weakness are bulbar involvement: baseline FVC, MIP and MEP stage the respiratory risk and serve as the reference if bulbar weakness progresses (Lawn ND et al., Arch Neurol 2001).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Increased jitter with blocking in frontalis
action_criteria.label: Single-fiber EMG (not needed when RNS is diagnostic)
action_criteria.rationale: RNS already shows a facial decrement with positive AChR antibodies; single-fiber EMG adds no diagnostic information but is not wasteful.

action_criteria.label: Review guidance on the management of generalized myasthenia gravis
action_criteria.rationale: Background reading on management; not a clinical step in the work-up.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not start high-dose prednisone (above 20 mg/day) as an outpatient; start low and titrate, or start high dose only with inpatient monitoring, because initial steroid-induced worsening can precipitate crisis.

Avoid fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, macrolides and IV magnesium unless no alternative exists and the patient is monitored; use non-depolarising neuromuscular blockers only at reduced dose with quantitative monitoring.
Do not attribute the fatigable hypophonia to functional dysphonia or muscle tension dysphonia before AChR antibody testing and neurophysiology.
required_recommendations: Diagnose AChR antibody-positive myasthenia gravis with predominantly bulbar (laryngeal and palatal) weakness, MGFA class IIb: fatigable hypophonia worse in the evening, normal laryngoscopy, AChR binding antibody 1.11 nmol/L, facial decrement on RNS, no thymoma.
Start pyridostigmine 30 mg three times daily, titrating to effect up to 60 mg four to five times daily; it may loosen her constipation, and diarrhea is a dose-related side effect.

If symptoms persist on pyridostigmine, add prednisone started low (10-20 mg/day, increasing by 5-10 mg every 3-7 days) with bone protection, and a steroid-sparing agent (azathioprine after TPMT testing) if long-term immunosuppression is needed [Sanders_2016].
Refer for thymectomy: AChR-positive generalized (bulbar) MG at age 53 without thymoma (MGTX) [Wolfe_2016].
Arrange speech and language therapy assessment of voice and swallowing, and advise her to seek care at once for choking, dysphagia or breathlessness.

avoided_actions.rationale: EEG has no role in a disorder of the neuromuscular junction (Jacob S et al., Pract Neurol 2025).
CSF has no role in MG (Jacob S et al., Pract Neurol 2025); no CNS or Miller Fisher alternative is raised here.
FDG-PET is not indicated in MG; mediastinal CT covers thymoma screening (Jacob S et al., Pract Neurol 2025).
No cardiac question in this patient; echocardiography does not contribute to the diagnosis of MG.
No palpitations, syncope or arrhythmia; cardiac monitoring does not contribute to the diagnosis of MG.

accepted: AChR antibody-positive myasthenia gravis with isolated pharyngeal/laryngeal presentation (hypophonia)

differential.diagnosis: Functional aphonia or muscle tension dysphonia
differential.key_features: Normal laryngoscopy and a normal examination at rest raised it, but the voice fades with sustained phonation and through the day, the palate is weak, and AChR antibodies and a facial RNS decrement are present.
Constipation and soft speech raised it, but there is no bradykinesia, rigidity or tremor, articulation is normal and the hypophonia is fatigable.
Fluctuating rather than fixed weakness and a normal laryngoscopy.
No tongue weakness, wasting or fasciculations, normal reflexes, fluctuating course and positive AChR antibodies.
Bulbar predominance fits the MuSK phenotype, but MuSK antibody is negative and AChR antibody positive.
Laryngoscopy showed no laryngeal pathology; the voice fluctuates.

key_clinical_evidence: Fifteen days of hypophonia, best on waking and near-inaudible by evening, with progressive volume decrement on sustained phonation and mild palatal weakness; limbs and eyes normal.
Outpatient laryngoscopy showed no laryngeal pathology.
AChR binding antibody 1.11 nmol/L with elevated blocking antibody; MuSK negative; thyroid function normal.
RNS: 13% decrement in nasalis and 11% in orbicularis oculi with none in ADM.
Mediastinal CT with contrast is indicated in every patient with MG to detect thymoma. Here it shows no thymoma, so thymectomy is indicated per MGTX at age 53.
Isolated laryngeal presentations of MG are easily mistaken for functional dysphonia; objective fatigability and serology separate them.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Constipation is longstanding slow-transit constipation; there is no parkinsonism on examination, and fatigable hypophonia with AChR antibodies and a facial decrement is MG, not Parkinson disease.
red_herrings.data_point: Chronic constipation raising concern for autonomic dysfunction or Parkinson's pre-motor symptoms
red_herrings.intended_effect: Constipation is a pre-motor feature of Parkinson's disease; combined with progressive voice changes, PD is considered

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Bulbar MG can show little at rest; fatigue on sustained phonation, mild palatal weakness, AChR antibodies and the RNS decrement establish an organic disorder of neuromuscular transmission.
red_herrings.data_point: Otherwise normal neurological examination at rest raising concern for a functional disorder
red_herrings.intended_effect: No weakness, no ptosis, entirely normal neurological exam might suggest functional hypophonia
red_herrings.location: history of present illness and exam

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: A normal laryngoscopy is expected in MG: transmission failure weakens the laryngeal muscles without structural change.
red_herrings.data_point: ENT referral with no structural laryngeal pathology
red_herrings.intended_effect: Normal laryngoscopy might suggest functional or psychological voice disorder

sequence_constraints.reason: AChR antibody testing precedes single-fiber EMG; SFEMG is reserved for seronegative patients or a normal RNS (Jacob 2025).
Repetitive nerve stimulation is done first; SFEMG follows when RNS is normal (Jacob 2025).

myasthenia gravis.query: myasthenia gravis diagnosis and treatment guidance

results.finding: Consensus guidance recommends AChR antibody testing first, MuSK testing when AChR antibodies are absent, and electrodiagnostic confirmation by repetitive nerve stimulation or single-fiber EMG. Chest CT or MRI is recommended in all patients to detect thymoma.
results.source: Sanders DB et al., Neurology 2016;87:419-425; Narayanaswami P et al., Neurology 2021;96:114-122

results.finding: In the MGTX trial thymectomy improved outcomes over three years in non-thymomatous AChR-positive generalized MG aged 18-65.
results.source: Wolfe GI et al., N Engl J Med 2016;375:511-522 (MGTX)

myasthenia gravis.summary: Consensus guidance (Sanders 2016; update Narayanaswami 2021): AChR antibody testing first, MuSK when AChR antibodies are absent, RNS or single-fiber EMG for electrodiagnostic confirmation, chest CT or MRI in all patients for thymoma. MGTX (Wolfe 2016): thymectomy improved three-year outcomes in non-thymomatous AChR-positive generalized MG aged 18-65.

mri.impression: Normal MRI of the brain, including the brainstem. No structural lesion identified.

patient.chief_complaint: Voice fading and near-inaudible speech by evening, 15 days duration

family_history: No family history of neuromuscular, autoimmune, or neurological disease

social_history.note: English language teacher; married; two adult children; non-smoker; non-drinker; physically active

patient.history_present_illness:
A 53-year-old Sri Lankan woman presented to the neurology ward with a 15-day history of progressive reduction in voice quality. She described her voice as initially having reduced tone and texture, likening it to sounding 'pressed' and 'soft.' The voice was markedly better upon waking in the morning and feeble but intelligible through the first half of the day, degrading to near-inaudibility by evening. Her husband could not hear her speaking from across the room by dinner time. She denied choking, coughing, aspiration, throat discomfort, or pain. She had a long-standing history of constipation attributed to slow bowel transit but was otherwise healthy. She did not smoke, did not drink alcohol, and had no family history of chronic illness or neurological disease.

She had been seen by an otolaryngology service as an outpatient; laryngoscopy showed no laryngeal pathology, and empirical treatment offered there produced no improvement. She presented to neurology with the ENT referral noting 'no structural cause identified.'

On examination, vital signs were normal. She was alert and conversational at baseline (morning examination). Neurological examination was otherwise normal: muscle strength 5/5 on the Medical Research Council scale across all tested groups, normal gait, tandem walk intact, gag reflex intact, all cranial nerves functional, and normal deep tendon reflexes bilaterally. Speech articulation was intact with normal tone and resonance, but markedly reduced volume and speech rate. Palate elevation was slightly weak but symmetric. Sustained speech testing over 2 minutes produced progressive reduction in volume from already soft baseline. A sustained 'ahh' for 20 seconds produced progressive volume decrement.

neurological_exam.coordination: Coordination normal. Normal gait and tandem walk.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Speech: low volume, slow rate, normal articulation and resonance. Palate elevation symmetric but mildly weak. Gag reflex intact. No tongue weakness, no fasciculations. Sustained vowel production: progressive volume decrement over 15-20 seconds. No ptosis. No diplopia. Normal extraocular movements. Cogan lid twitch negative.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert; oriented x3. No cognitive impairment.

No tongue weakness, no fasciculations. Sustained vowel production: progressive volume decrement over 15-20 seconds. No ptosis. No diplopia. Normal extraocular movements. Cogan lid twitch negative.
